**Statements:**

All carroms are ludos.

All ludos are scrabbles.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some carroms are not scrabbles.

II. Some scrabbles are carroms.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e8fc5e492cbfaa49cc6159d1bef107de52421c68c44d0bbe881659536d3f24c.png] 

Conclusions:

I) Some carroms are not scrabbles → Does not follow (As all carroms are ludos and all ludos are scrabbles. As whole carroms comes in ludos which whole comes in scrabbles, thus whole carroms are scrabbles, therefore it is false.)

II) Some scrabbles are carroms → Follow (As all carroms are ludos and all ludos are scrabbles. As whole carroms comes in ludos which whole comes in scrabbles, therefore it is true)

∴ Here, Only conclusion II ​follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1"

All scanners are printers.

Some scanners are copiers.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy comes under which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 36 - 51.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy **(DPSP) come under Articles 36 to 51 of the Indian Constitution. **
 
• These principles serve as **guidelines for the government **to follow while framing laws and policies, aimed at establishing a just society in India.
 
• Although these principles are **non-justiciable** (not enforceable by the courts), they are** fundamental in the governance** of the country.
 
• The DPSPs aim to promote social and economic welfare, including provisions for equal pay for equal work, securing a living wage, free legal aid, and promoting education and public health **(Article 39, 41, 42).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Articles 12 – 35: Fundamental Rights**

__
 
• **Article 12**: Defines the term State for the purpose of enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It includes the government, Parliament, state legislatures, and other authorities.
 
• **Article 13**: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights are void.
 
• **Articles 14-18**: The Right to Equality covers equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination, and abolition of untouchability.
 
• **Articles 19-22**: The Right to Freedom covers speech, assembly, movement, protection in respect of conviction for offenses, and protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• **Articles 23-24**: Protection against exploitation, including human trafficking and forced labor.
 
• **Articles 25-28**: The Right to Freedom of Religion includes freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• **Articles 29-30**: Rights related to Cultural and Educational Freedoms for minorities.
 
• **Articles 31-35**: Include provisions for the Right to Property (later removed as a Fundamental Right), and the Right to Constitutional Remedies under Article 32.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 34: Restriction on Rights during Martial Law**

 
 
• Allows Parliament to impose restrictions on fundamental rights when martial law is in force.
 
• Provides legal protection for acts done under martial law to maintain law and order.
 
 
 
• **Article 35: Legislation for Part III Provisions**
 
 
• Grants Parliament the power to make laws for enforcing certain Fundamental Rights (e.g., abolition of untouchability, prohibition of trafficking).
 
• Ensures Parliament alone can legislate on these matters to maintain uniformity across India.

• It consists of two sets of smooth muscles: the **sphincter pupillae** (which constricts the pupil) and the **dilator pupillae** (which dilates the pupil).
 
• The iris plays a** crucial** role in adapting to different lighting conditions by controlling pupil size, helping to protect the retina from excessive light, and improving vision in varying light conditions.

questions.question: The concept of limited government is a major advancement to protect the _________ of the citizens from the ruling governments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fundamental rights.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A limited government is **restricted by a constitution** and **cannot act arbitrarily or override the constitution**. This prevents the government from threatening the rights of the people.
 
• A limited government's main** function is to protect people and their property.** 
 
• Fundamental rights** act as a check** on the power of the government.
 
• The Fundamental Rights of the Indian Constitution are covered in **Articles 12 to 35 of Part III **of the Constitution.
 
 
• **Right to equality**: Articles 14–18
 
• **Right to freedom**: Articles 19–22
 
• **Right against exploitation**: Articles 23–24
 
• **Right to freedom of religion**: Articles 25–28
 
• **Cultural and educational rights**: Articles 29–30
 
• **Right to constitutional remedies**: Article 32
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **separation of powers** in India is the **division of the government's legislative, executive, and judicial functions** into separate branches.

 
 
• **Articles 122 and 212**:- These articles prevent the judiciary from interfering with the legislative process by not allowing courts to inquire into the proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures. 
 
• **Articles 105 and 194**:- These articles prohibit courts from calling members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies to testify about speeches they made in those houses.
 
• **Article 13**:- This article gives the judiciary the power of judicial review, allowing it to strike down any law that it deems unconstitutional or arbitrary. 
 
• **Article 50**:- This article encourages the separation of the judiciary from the executive.
 
 
 
• The Indian Constitution uses the principle of** checks and balances** to distribute power among the three branches of government, the legislature, executive, and judiciary, to ensure accountability and prevent any one branch from becoming too powerful.
 
 
• **Legislative and executive**:- The **President can summon**, prorogue, and dissolve Parliament. Parliament can** impeach the President** for violating the Constitution.
 
• **Executive and judiciary**:- The executive branch appoints judges to the higher judiciary, including the Supreme Court and High Courts. The judiciary can **review the executive's actions** through judicial review.
 
 
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** of Indian citizens are listed in **Article 51A of Part IV-A **of the Constitution and were added by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976.**
 
 
• **​** The purpose of the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution is to remind** citizens of their responsibilities to the nation **and each other and to uphold the values of the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties aim **to promote harmony and brotherhood** among all citizens, transcending regional, linguistic, and religious differences.

questions.question: Which of the following scientists grouped the elements into triads?

__
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner, a German chemist,** was one of the first to classify elements based on their similar properties.
 
• In 1829, **he observed that certain groups of three elements had similar chemical properties **and
 
 
• that the atomic mass of the middle element was roughly the average of the other two.
 
 
 
• These **groups of three elements became known as "Döbereiner’s Triads."**
 
• **For example**:
 
 
• Lithium, Sodium, Potassium: In this triad, sodium’s atomic mass is the average of lithium and potassium.
 
• Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine: These elements also formed a triad with similar chemical behavior.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Newlands**

 
 
• **Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves**, where he arranged elements in increasing order of atomic mass and noticed that every eighth element had similar properties.
 
• His **work was an important step toward the development of the modern periodic table,** but it was initially criticized for not being applicable to all elements.
 
• His classification system was later recognized as a precursor to Mendeleev’s work.
 
 
 
• **Henry Moseley**
 
 
• Moseley **established the concept of atomic numb**er, which is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• His work showed that elements are better arranged by increasing atomic number rather than atomic mass, leading to a more accurate periodic table.
 
• **His research resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev’s periodic table.**
 
 
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**

questions.question: Which of the following organisms can initiate ecological succession even in bare rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lichens.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lichens are considered **pioneer species**, meaning they are among the first organisms to colonize bare rocks.
 
• Lichens secrete acids that slowly **break down rocks**, leading to the formation of soil, making it possible for other plants to grow.
 
• Lichens consist of fungi and algae (or cyanobacteria) living in a **symbiotic relationship**, allowing them to survive in harsh conditions.
 
• They are extremely** resilient** and can survive in extreme **environmental conditions**, such as high altitudes and exposed rock surfaces.
 
• **Soil formation:** By breaking down rock and accumulating organic material, lichens contribute to the creation of the first layer of soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Orchids:**

 
• Orchids often grow on **other plants** (such as trees) without harming them, known as epiphytes, and are not capable of growing directly on bare rocks.
 
• Orchids typically appear in more advanced stages of **ecological succession** when the environment is more hospitable, with developed soil and host plants.
 
• They thrive in humid environments with specific light, moisture, and nutrient conditions, relying on **organic material** rather than barren environments.

**Aspergillus:**

 
• Aspergillus is a genus of **fungi **that decomposes organic matter and grows in a variety of environments, but it does not colonize bare rocks.
 
• This fungus breaks down already existing **organic matter**, such as dead plants or animals, and is more common in later stages of succession.
 
• Certain species of Aspergillus can cause **diseases** in plants and animals, including humans (e.g., aspergillosis in humans).

**Lily:**

 
• Lilies are **angiosperms** (flowering plants) that require a developed soil layer rich in nutrients, water, and light to grow.
 
• They appear in ecosystems where soil formation has already occurred, indicating that they are not **pioneer** species.
 
• Lilies grow in **wetlands** or well-drained, nutrient-rich soils and cannot survive in barren or rocky environments.

questions.question: In a sweet, one-third is sugar. If the price of sugar now is (7)/(6) of the previous price, what is the effective percentage increase in the cost of the sweet?

Cost of sugar in sweet = dfrac{1}{3} units

Cost of other ingredients = 1 - dfrac{1}{3} = dfrac{2}{3} units

New price of sugar = dfrac{7}{6} × dfrac{1}{3} = dfrac{7}{18} units

New cost of sweet = dfrac{7}{18} + dfrac{2}{3}

⇒ New cost of sweet = dfrac{7}{18} + dfrac{12}{18} = dfrac{19}{18} units

Effective percentage increase in cost = dfrac{dfrac{19}{18} - 1}{1} times 100

⇒ Effective percentage increase in cost = dfrac{1}{18} times 100

questions.question: Two trains, P and Q, are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with lengths of 110 m and 140 m, respectively. Train P is running at a speed of 70 km/h and took 5 seconds to cross train Q. The speed of train Q is:
